questions.question: Which African country has the highest population?
questions.fun_fact: Nigeria is the most populous nation in Africa and the sixth most populous in the world.

questions.question: What is the powerhouse of the cell responsible for generating most of the chemical energy needed?
questions.fun_fact: Mitochondria contain their own distinct DNA separate from the rest of the cell.

questions.question: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall, marking a symbolic end to the Cold War?
questions.fun_fact: The fall of the Berlin Wall on November 9, 1989, paved the way for the reunification of Germany.

questions.question: Which 1994 animated Disney film features the song 'Circle of Life'?
questions.fun_fact: Elton John and Tim Rice composed the legendary music for The Lion King.

questions.question: Which spice, known as the most expensive in the world by weight, comes from the threads of the Crocus sativus flower?
questions.fun_fact: It takes approximately 75,000 saffron blossoms to harvest just a single pound of saffron spice.

questions.question: What is the primary diet of a giant panda?
questions.fun_fact: Giant pandas spend up to 12 hours a day chewing and eating bamboo to meet their daily nutritional needs.

questions.question: How many players are on the pitch for a single team in a standard association football (soccer) match?
questions.fun_fact: The 11-player rule per team has been a standard regulation in association football since the late 19th century.

questions.question: What is the term for a word or phrase that reads the same backward as forward, ignoring spaces and punctuation?
questions.fun_fact: A classic English sentence palindrome is 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'.

questions.question: Which planet in our solar system is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.fun_fact: Mars gets its reddish color from the large amount of iron oxide, or rust, on its surface.

questions.question: Who was the brilliant English mathematician and cryptanalyst who led the team that cracked the Enigma code at Bletchley Park during World War II?
questions.fun_fact: Alan Turing's pioneering work in theoretical computer science laid the foundation for modern computing and artificial intelligence.
